answer: Require independent hands on the pen. High-value actions — minting credit, moving large balances, certifying a new identity — need k-of-n co-signatures from identities the ledger scores as independent: distinct histories, vantages, vintages. A farm’s thousand wallets can sign, but the diversity check sees one vine around a trellis, and the quill will not move without separate hands. The operator must find strangers — hands as free as zephyr, not buyable or cornerable — to co-sign, and strangers can audit, refuse, or report. Centralized control becomes unexecutable, not just discouraged.
